column1: # People READ from a register act who are in no family file. One row per (name, act). See tools/read_names.py.
# name   the name as the page prints it, given name(s) first. When the author's text gives the surname first
#        and the order is not certain, the name is left as written (Candeloro Benedetto).
# form   the form the register or the notes print, when it is the surname-first one ("Minasi Francesco"). It
#        becomes an alias, so the build-time linker finds both.
# as     child, deceased, groom, bride, parent, witness, official, declarant, other
# role   what the act calls them (completes "<role> <of>")
# of     the other person(s) in the act the role is about
# kind   Nati, Matrimoni, Morti, Pubblicazioni, Processetti   year   the act's year   no   the act number
# age    the age the ACT gives, a number or empty. It, and the year, are all the living rule is given.
# ark    the Antenati ark of the volume, from the archive's own tables (checked against them) or empty
# cite   the citation, when it is not simply "<comune>, <kind> <year>, atto <no>"
# page   the narrative page (and section) where the act is discussed
# from   the row of the archive's own data this rests on, checked by tools/check_read_names.py:
#          scilla-reads:<year>/<act>   a row of data/scilla-reads.tsv     register-reads:<plate>   data/register-reads.tsv
#          pe-mazza-acts:<year>/<act>  data/pe-mazza-acts.tsv             sicily-reads:<who>       a row of data/sicily-reads.tsv, by its first words
#          page:<name>                 the narrative page itself (a name the page prints from the act it describes)
# Nothing here is a person's page. A name page says who was read under the name and where; it never says two
# acts are one man. Nobody is on it whom the living rule cannot show to be dead from the act's year and age.
